claims.claim: Users are registered accounts with access to the frontend, the backend or both.
Users can be created from the frontend by Extranet and Create user apps.
The Shopping Cart app can create users during checkout.
The Forms for Editors app can create users when a form is submitted.
Users can be created under a user group or via integration.
Permissions control access to backend areas and frontend content; frontend users have Read by default.
Frontend content can be restricted to logged-in users by setting Anonymous users (frontend) to None.
A user has one default address and can have additional addresses created from the frontend, backend or integration.
Custom address fields can extend addresses.
Backend free-text user search runs over a fixed column set.

excluded.reason: Admin UI search box; no persisted state for a build to apply or prove.

claims.claim: Any user list can be exported to Excel with column-header presets from export templates.

excluded.reason: Admin UI action with no persisted outcome on the solution; not a demo build function.

claims.claim: Groups are nested and organise users, set permissions and share settings.
Users can add or remove themselves from selected groups through the Extranet app.
A group representing a customer should be an account.
A group can carry a default permission for its members.
Group customer number and email let the Create user app place new users in the matching group.
A segment search query on a group makes membership dynamic.
Groups with a custom group type have an Addresses tab.
Group custom field values are stored on the group and not copied to members.
Allow backend login on a group applies to members and subgroups.
Redirect after login, item type and default user item type can be set on a group.

excluded.reason: Per-group presentation settings with no independent demo outcome; covered by the content and Swift areas where used.

claims.claim: Disable live prices and live discounts on a group.
Group latitude, longitude, custom geolocation and map icon.
Users can be imported into a group, for example with the User provider.
The user overview shows groups, addresses, impersonation, latest logins and profiles.
A user has username, password, type, active state and an authentication method override.
The per-user authentication method overrides the solution login type.
Allow backend login on a user, read-only when inherited from a group.
Custom user fields appear on a Fields tab.
Additional addresses are managed on the Addresses tab with active, kind and default.
Advanced tab: role, item type, redirect, external ID, active from and to.
Advanced tab: geolocation settings.
Advanced tab: disable live prices and discounts.
Commerce tab: customer number, price and discount group, default shop, currency and stock location.
Send user details email with a fixed tag set.

excluded.reason: One-off admin action; no persisted outcome to prove.

claims.claim: Send a recovery mail and set a password from the action menu.

excluded.reason: One-off admin action; no persisted outcome to prove.

claims.claim: Review changes made to the user.
Addresses are shared between users with the same customer number through app settings.
Shopping cart Retrieve delivery addresses can offer addresses of users with the same customer number.
Headless storefronts share addresses through the includeAddressesFromUsersWithSameCustomerNumber parameter.
Sign-in depends on active state, validity dates and authentication method; sign-ins are logged.
Login users and customer profiles let one person buy for several customers.
The Authentication app can show a profile selector after sign-in.
System user types Administrator, Admin and Editor with default access.
Custom user and group types can be created.
Accounts represent a customer company and need the Enable user account functionality feature.
Users are added to an account by creation, by matching customer number, by the User provider or by a segment search.
The frontend relies on the customer number, not on account membership.
Accounts own addresses that buyers can use but not change.
Account addresses reach users only through the shared address source.
Account Advanced tab mirrors group settings (tree section, redirect, backend login, item types, external ID, geolocation, live prices).
Imported addresses link to their owner through AccessUserAddressUserID; link by external ID.
Create user app can auto-assign a customer number and add the user to the matching account.
Login activity lists backend and frontend sign-in events with method, result, reason and IP.
Login entries can open, edit or deactivate the user.
Latest logins widget and logins-per-week graph on the user overview.
Entries are deleted after retention by the Clean up login log task.
Users or groups can act on behalf of other users or groups for assisted selling.
Impersonation relations are set on the user manually or by integration, in both directions.
Selecting a group makes all its users impersonators or impersonable.
Permission levels Not set, None, Read, Edit, Create, Delete, All form a hierarchy; highest wins.
Older solutions may still use the previous model where None was an explicit deny.

excluded.reason: Legacy permission model; DW10 demos are built on the current model only.

claims.claim: User roles supply defaults: anonymous and authenticated frontend Read, backend Not set, administrators All.
Denying Anonymous users (frontend) on a branch creates a members area.
Explicit permissions are set per item from the Permissions workspace, including turning an inherited row explicit.
A query can be selected as a permission principal.
UI permissions (10.21+) hide areas and navigation sections without changing authorisation.
Product permissions are inherited from the product group or the Products area.
Product attribute permissions limit attributes to None, Read or Edit.
Content, PIM and commerce manager role examples.
Permissions on shops, warehouses, groups and ecommerce languages.
Shop and channel permissions limit order management lists and filters.
Coordinates are calculated from the address through Google Maps on request.
Custom geolocation blocks automatic updates.
Geolocation is exposed through item fields on users and groups.
User queries can retrieve sets such as all active users and make group membership dynamic.
The All Users system query lists every user.

excluded.reason: Built-in system query present on every solution; no build choice to prove.

claims.claim: Segment searches filter users by user, audit, behaviour, email marketing and custom fields.
Segment search membership is applied only after the Calculate user segment search results task runs.
User-area queries are index queries on a user index.
Custom user fields with typed values and options.
Custom address fields with typed values and options.
Frontend login type: normal, TOTP, magic link or MFA, with code validity.
Extranet login limitations: attempts per period and blocking period.
Frontend recovery token timeout and login cookie lifetime.
Password expiration, reuse, complexity and minimum length for backend and frontend.
Presets screen has no function and is pending deletion.

claims.claim: Backend login type: normal, TOTP, magic link or MFA.
Default send-user-details subject, sender and template.

claims.claim: Auto build a user index when users update.
Custom user and group types with parent restrictions, stored under Files/System/UserTypes.
External login providers for Azure AD B2C, GitHub, Google, Microsoft Entra, Entra External ID and Okta, for backend, frontend or both.
Handle only external verification disables creating users on first external sign-in; new users can be placed in groups.
Backend users must exist and are matched by email; frontend providers must be added to the login template.
Users area settings overview.

claims.claim: Users apps reimplement the Extranet tasks with ViewModels.
Authentication app lets users log in.
Change password app for signed-in users.
Create user app with email activation.
Edit user app updates or deletes the own account.
Forgot password app sends a recovery link.
Manage addresses app lists, edits and creates addresses, optionally of users with the same customer number.
View user app lists users by group, customer number or impersonation, or shows one user.
Extranet app creates profiles with approval and notification emails.
Extranet app handles log in, password change and recovery, redirect after login.
Extranet app views and edits profiles and manages addresses.
Extranet app publishes lists of users or groups.

excluded.reason: Directory listing is a presentation choice owned by the Swift building area; no independent acceptance.

claims.claim: Clean up login log task deletes entries older than the retention days (default 365).

gaps: Accounts feature flag key (Feature Management > User Accounts > Enable user account functionality) is not verified, so it is not declared in requires.
Login security settings (login type, password policy, login limitations) live in the global settings file; key names and a settings-file handler are missing, so both checks are planned only.
Shopping cart app setting Retrieve delivery addresses: settings key not observed, so the shared-address check reads only the Manage addresses app.
Clean up login log add-in type name not verified; its check has no SQL binding.
The 'SystemAccount' group type and the ListUserProfiles / Source setting values were observed on a 10.29.x baseline database; no public DW source confirms them.
Swift customer-center pages for account administrators managing colleague users are not covered by the manual pages read; owned by the Swift building area if added.
The All Users system query, Export to Excel and Send user details are excluded as admin UI actions without a demo outcome.

Checks offered to the owners of duplicated functions, not authored here: the group gate pair (AuthenticatedFrontend None plus a group Read on the same entity) and a per-persona refusal proof for content.page-permissions; the storefront switch proof for commerce.sales-on-behalf.
